passage.text: Depression is the way in which a person experiences the loss of hope when their repeated attempts to reach the other person have failed. It can be understood as a co-constructed relational phenomenon with three intrinsic and essential features. The first is a profound attachment, in which the other is deeply loved and felt to be necessary. The second is the failure of all efforts to reach that other person. The third is the emotional absence of the other from the relationship.

source.title: Article Aesthetic Diagnosis in Gestalt Therapy

taps.prompt: What is the main idea of the text?
taps.correct: Depression emerges from failed attempts to connect with someone deeply loved whose emotional withdrawal creates hopelessness.
wrong: Depression results from a person's inability to love others deeply enough.
Depression is caused by the other person intentionally rejecting connection.
taps.explain: The excerpt defines depression as a relational pattern, not individual pathology.

taps.context: The third is the emotional absence of the other from the relationship.
taps.explain: 'The other' refers to the person who is emotionally unavailable in the relationship.

taps.correct: A person becomes depressed after repeatedly failing to connect with someone they love.

A person loses hope before attempting to reach the other person.
taps.explain: The paraphrase captures the causal sequence: repeated failed attempts cause hopelessness.
